the TCR repertoire in accepted graft is skewed toward a few dominant T cell clones, which may represent a regulatory T cell population.
the TCR repertoire is a useful parameter to monitor the immune response against allogeneic solid organ transplants.

, in the absence of immunosuppressive drugs, the TCR Vβ profile of the T cells invading accepted kidneys is skewed and dominated by a few clones, which progressively intensify their preeminence with time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of immunosuppressants, a short period of T cell activation is sufficient to induce a long-term tolerance in a class I-disparate allogeneic kidney transplant.
the intragraft T cell population is composed of a small number of dominant clones that may be involved in graft tolerance.
the TCRβ CDR3 length polymorphism can be a powerful tool to assess the clonal composition of T cell infiltrates in solid organ transplants.
